B. Is this measure already running in Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital. Every patient whose cancer has not spread (stage I-III) is discussed by video with the university hospital lung team (surgeon, radiotherapy doctor, oncologist) before anyone decides against treatment that aims to cure. Today a county hospital can decide alone.
effect_summary_en: One UK before-after study (62 patients in one year) found that the annual resection rate rose by 30% (relative) after video MDT meetings started; it reports no change in the share of all patients who got curative treatment.
supported_en: A 2004 UK study (Davison et al., J Telemed Telecare) reports a 30% relative rise in resections after video MDT meetings started.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the assumed 1.5-point rise in the curative share, or any effect in a setting like HUS, where the lung team is already in the same organisation.
in_use_quote: Tarvittaessa arvioimme syövän tilanteen ja annamme hoitosuosituksen HUSin moniammatillisessa keuhkosyövän diagnostiikkaan ja hoitoon perehtyneiden erikoislääkäreiden työryhmässä.
in_use_summary_en: HUS, which runs Peijas hospital and treats patients from Vantaa and Kerava, says its lung cancer pathway has a multidisciplinary specialist team that reviews cases and gives a treatment recommendation "when needed" (page updated 15.06.2026).
missing_en: No page shows that every stage I–III patient must be reviewed by the HUS lung team before curative treatment is ruled out.
summary_en: HUS, which treats Vantaa and Kerava lung cancer patients, says its multidisciplinary lung cancer specialist team reviews cases and gives a treatment recommendation when needed. No page says every stage I–III patient must be reviewed. The only effect evidence read is one UK before-after study, which found a 30% relative rise in resections after video MDT meetings started; this is weaker than the assumed effect and comes from a different setting.
unanswered_en: I found nothing showing whether HUS reviews every stage I–III patient, or how many patients decided at Peijas go without the team's review.
